title: Two players,
subtitle: twelve bytes a message.
summary: Lockstep multiplayer with fizlet/presence and the rooms server on Cloudflare: what is shipped, how to run it, and its caps.
lead: `fizlet/presence` is lockstep input exchange: every peer runs the same fixed-step sim from the same seed, and only inputs cross the wire, 12 bytes a message. The room server in [`rooms/` ↗](https://github.com/coded-dot-design/fizlet/tree/main/rooms) is a Cloudflare Worker with one Durable Object per room that seats players and relays their messages. It never simulates. This guide connects the two.

items.title: Deterministic step
items.body: Seeded random, no clock, no layout reads, state in typed arrays. [Determinism](/docs/determinism/) has the rules.

items.title: One input word per player
items.body: Pack what a player does into 32 bits: keys as bits, a pointer in fractions of a fixed arena. The step reads the words, never the local controls.

items.title: Check it before the network
items.body: `syncCheck` runs your sim as lockstep clients over an in-memory link with latency and jitter, and names the first frame that differs.

items: Your input for a frame is sent `delay` frames ahead (default 2: 33 ms at 60 Hz), so on a good link the game never waits.
A frame runs only when every player's input for it is in. A missing input stalls the sim (`net.stalls`); it never guesses, so peers can't drift.
State hashes cross every 30 frames (`hashEvery`). `net.desync` is the first frame whose hash differed, or -1.

Inputs live in fixed rings of typed arrays: `net.confirmed(slot, frame)` is the input log a rollback layer could replay. Presence adds no allocation to the steady state: its test counts young-generation GCs over 2 × 200k frames, with and without it.

body.text: The server is its own package in `rooms/`, not a dependency of `fizlet`. Locally it runs on `wrangler dev`: `npm install`, `npm test` (caps, invite keys, relay logic), then `npm run test:wrangler`, which starts a local Worker and plays two Fizlet engines through one room for 600 lockstep frames, byte-identical. Deploying to your own Cloudflare account is yours to do: [DEPLOY.md ↗](https://github.com/coded-dot-design/fizlet/blob/main/rooms/DEPLOY.md).

Each room seats players in arrival order and sends each a WELCOME (seat, player count, one shared seed) once it is full; `join(url)` resolves then. WebSockets use the hibernation API, so an idle room holds no running object, and rooms store nothing.

blocks.heading: 4. Caps in code
blocks.subhead: Every cap has a default and a ceiling in `rooms/src/limits.js`. Your config can lower a cap; nothing lifts it past its ceiling.

items.title: Rooms and seats
items.body: 16 rooms by default (ceiling 256), 2 players a room (ceiling 8).

items.title: Messages
items.body: 90 a second a socket, bursts to 180 (ceilings 240 and 480); lockstep at 60 Hz sends about 62. Over it, the socket closes with 1008. Anything but a 12-byte message closes it with 1009.

items.title: Time
items.body: A room with no message for 120 s closes (ceiling 3,600 s), and every room closes after 1,800 s (ceiling 14,400 s).

items.title: Who may join
items.body: An invite code checked against hashes in Workers KV (a demo gate, not a login), and `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`: the page origins allowed to connect.

items.a: Real accounts (the invite gate is a demo gate), a policy for a seat that leaves mid-game (today the others wait), and an authoritative room for games that need one.

items.q: Does a game need its own server code?
items.a: No. The room only seats, seeds and relays. The game logic runs in every browser, the same on each.

seo.title: Lockstep multiplayer rooms with Fizlet
seo.description: Run two-player lockstep games with fizlet/presence and a Cloudflare Worker room server: 12-byte inputs, a hash check every 30 frames and hard caps in code.
